title: Protocol for analyzing enzymatic hydrolysis of cellulose using surface pitting observation technology
protocol: Prepare 2× buffer of the target reaction buffer.
Pour 20 mL of 2× buffer into a Petri dish containing the nanofibrous cellulose plate.
Leave the plate for 1–4 h with gentle shaking on an orbital shaker.
Remove excess buffer with a pipette.
Store the nanofibrous cellulose in airtight Tupperware containers at 4°C.
Cut the disc-shaped cellulose plate into square pieces (1–3 cm across).
Place a piece of cellulose on a glass slide.
Air dry the cellulose plate for 20–30 min to remove excess water on the surface.
Enter the thickness value of the nanofibrous cellulose and glass slide into the material thickness parameter in the stage control panel of the inkjet device.
Maintain standardized air-drying conditions to obtain consistent pit-formation results.
Air dry for 20–30 minutes to allow enzymes to diffuse into cellulose matrices properly.
Proceed to the next steps while the gel is air drying.
Keep the time of enzyme deposition constant after removing the gel from the airtight container.
Deposit a solution containing 10 mg/mL cellulases (Meicelase) onto a flat surface of a nanofibrous cellulose gel using an inkjet patterning device equipped with an IJHBS 10 inkjet head.
Turn on the laser microscope for 60 minutes before use.
Mount the slide glass with nanofibrous cellulose on the sample stage base.
Set the distance from the nozzle tip of the inkjet print head to the surface of the nanofibrous cellulose gel to 1 mm.
Set the interval between droplets (dot spacing) to 400 μm.
Set the number of shots to be deposited; for example, 2 (0.18 ng of cellulases), 4 (0.36 ng), 6 (0.72 ng), or 8 shots (0.90 ng).
Include the droplet observation method to check the droplet performance.
Set a test condition outside the print area because the first shot is not stable.
Start patterning and check the droplet performance.
If issues are encountered with the proper ejection of drops from the inkjet nozzle, refer to troubleshooting for possible solutions.
Quantify pits on the surface of nanofibrous cellulose matrices using a laser scanning confocal microscope operated in reflection mode.
Obtain three-dimensional height maps of the pitted surface non-destructively.
Set the lens heater temperature to 40°C.
Wait for more than 10 minutes until the set temperature is reached.
Move to the spot position to be measured.
Mount nanofibrous cellulose on the stage of the microscope.
Place a glass slide to a defined place on the stage using double-sided tape.
Cover the nanofibrous cellulose and objective lens with a humidifying chamber.
Adjust the focal position to view the target area.
Determine the z range by moving the peak to the top and bottom of the target.
Save the peak information in memory.
Take panoramic images of 4 views (2 × 2 grids).
Repeat major steps until the end of the incubation period (30 min).
Export image files for further analysis.
Import an image file into the SPIP software.
Perform polynomial plane correction (flattening).
Select the pit using Area of Interest marking tools (Circle markers).
Calculate the fit surface for plane correction based on data outside the marked area.
Open the Plane Correction Dialog and apply settings from Table 3.
Generate the height distribution histogram automatically by the SPIP software.
Select volumes below the threshold (-1 μm) in the Histogram window.
